fastest_promotion_path.solar_faster_because: 0 data discrepancies to resolve (LOW effort step skipped)

portfolio_recommendation.rationale: Shared methodology dominates the critical path. Excel reference acquisition and parity computation are the same effort for both generics. Doing them in parallel halves calendar time. Per-project work is small relative to shared work. Governance is symmetric. Wind's 3 data discrepancies are LOW effort, not HIGH. Solar's 0 data discrepancies are a free simplification, not a strategic advantage. Sequential approaches risk perpetually deprioritizing the second generic.
portfolio_recommendation.why_not_A_wind_first: Wind has 3 LOW effort data discrepancies; this is the only 'extra' work for Wind, not enough to justify Wind-first sequencing.
portfolio_recommendation.why_not_B_solar_first: Solar has 0 data discrepancies; this is the only 'fewer steps' argument, symmetric to Wind-first. Neither is recommended over parallel.
portfolio_recommendation.why_C_parallel_strongest: Dominant cost (Excel reference + parity) is shared. Per-project costs are MEDIUM effort and can be done in parallel. Governance boundary is symmetric.
portfolio_recommendation.caveat: If capacity is constrained, A (Wind-first) is the next-best alternative because Wind's 3 discrepancies are a real work argument.

1st.rationale: Already at Level 2. No promotion work needed.

2nd.rationale: Already at Level 2. No promotion work needed.

3rd.rationale: Closer to Reference than Solar in terms of test coverage (18 vs 8+) and factory granularity. 3 data discrepancies to resolve.

4th.rationale: Same readiness as Wind. Lower test coverage (8+). 0 data discrepancies to resolve.

readiness_ranking.tie_breaker_Wind_vs_Solar: Generic Wind ranks 3rd, Generic Solar ranks 4th, based on test coverage. Wind has 18 incidental test references; Solar has 8+. The 10-file delta suggests Wind has more existing test surface to build a dedicated test pack on, which is a soft advantage for migration.

rationale: Shared methodology dominates the critical path. Excel reference acquisition and parity computation are the same effort for both generics. Doing them in parallel halves calendar time and reduces methodology risk.
Per-project work is small relative to shared work. Test pack, KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md, and D1/D2 redo/D3 redo rows must be done twice, but each is MEDIUM effort, not HIGH.
Governance is symmetric. Both generics are excluded from Pilot RC with the same wording (docs/pilot_rc_scope_matrix.md:27-28). The migration should be symmetric.
Wind's 3 data discrepancies are LOW effort, not HIGH. They do not justify a Wind-first sequencing.
Solar's 0 data discrepancies are a 'free' simplification, not a strategic advantage. They simply skip one LOW effort step.
Sequential approaches (Wind-first or Solar-first) risk perpetually deprioritizing the second generic. Parallel prevents this.

suggested_roadmap.F2-D: Excel reference acquisition + parity computation for BOTH Generic Wind and Generic Solar in parallel. For Wind, includes data discrepancy resolution. For Solar, just Excel reference + parity.
suggested_roadmap.F2-E: Test pack + KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md + D1/D2 redo/D3 redo rows for BOTH generics in parallel.
suggested_roadmap.F2-F: Phase 51F parity green + Pilot RC scope matrix CI guard for BOTH generics in parallel.
suggested_roadmap.F2-G: Promotion gate evaluation for BOTH generics, run independently. Generic Wind and Generic Solar can be promoted to Level 2 in the same F-phase or in separate F-phases, depending on the gate outcome.

stop_after_report_contract.next_phase_start: F2-D (Excel reference + parity, both generics in parallel). F2-E, F2-F, F2-G follow in their own follow-up prompts.
stop_after_report_contract.rationale: F2-C is a comparison + critical-path analysis only. F2-D begins the actual preparation work, gated on F2-C review.
